interactions.mechanism: Ashwagandha stimulates thyroid hormone synthesis and conversion of T4 to T3
interactions.clinical_effect: May increase thyroid hormone levels beyond therapeutic range, causing hyperthyroid symptoms (palpitations, weight loss, anxiety)
interactions.management: Monitor thyroid function tests every 4-6 weeks if combining. May need dose reduction of thyroid medication.

interactions.mechanism: Ashwagandha potentiates immune system activity via T-cell and NK-cell stimulation
interactions.clinical_effect: May counteract immunosuppression, risking organ rejection in transplant patients
interactions.management: Avoid in transplant patients. Consult specialist before use with any immunosuppressant.

interactions.mechanism: Ashwagandha has GABAergic and CNS depressant properties (withanolides bind GABA receptors)
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced sedation, excessive drowsiness, impaired coordination
interactions.management: Use with caution. Avoid driving or operating machinery. Consider reducing sedative dose.

interactions.mechanism: Ashwagandha has hypoglycemic activity through insulin sensitization
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced blood sugar lowering — may cause hypoglycemia
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose closely. May allow reduction of antidiabetic medication dose under medical supervision.

interactions.mechanism: Ashwagandha has mild vasodilatory and BP-lowering properties
interactions.clinical_effect: Additive blood pressure lowering — may cause dizziness or fainting
interactions.management: Monitor blood pressure. Generally safe but watch for hypotensive symptoms.

interactions.mechanism: Curcumin inhibits platelet aggregation, thromboxane synthesis, and potentiates anticoagulant effects. May also inhibit CYP2C9 which metabolizes warfarin.
interactions.clinical_effect: Significantly increased bleeding risk — bruising, prolonged bleeding, potentially internal bleeding
interactions.management: Avoid high-dose turmeric supplements (>500mg curcumin/day) with blood thinners. Dietary turmeric in cooking is generally safe. Monitor INR if on warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Curcumin improves insulin sensitivity and has hypoglycemic effects
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced blood sugar lowering — hypoglycemia risk
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose. Usually beneficial but dose adjustment may be needed.

interactions.mechanism: Turmeric increases stomach acid production and stimulates bile flow
interactions.clinical_effect: May reduce effectiveness of acid-reducing medications in some cases
interactions.management: Generally safe in moderate doses. Monitor symptoms.

interactions.mechanism: Curcumin may interfere with chemotherapy by reducing cancer cell sensitivity to drugs through antioxidant mechanisms
interactions.clinical_effect: May reduce effectiveness of chemotherapy — tumor cells may not be killed properly
interactions.management: Avoid curcumin supplements during chemotherapy. Discuss with oncologist before use.

interactions.mechanism: Neem has potent hypoglycemic activity — multiple mechanisms including insulin secretion stimulation and glucose utilization improvement
interactions.clinical_effect: Severe hypoglycemia — blood sugar may drop dangerously low. Can cause loss of consciousness.
interactions.management: Do NOT combine with diabetes medications without strict medical supervision. Monitor blood glucose frequently if used together.

interactions.mechanism: Neem stimulates immune function — may counteract immunosuppression
interactions.clinical_effect: Reduced immunosuppressive effect — risk of organ rejection
interactions.management: Avoid in transplant patients and those requiring immunosuppression.

interactions.mechanism: Neem has documented antifertility effects — may reduce sperm count and motility, disrupt female reproductive cycle
interactions.clinical_effect: May counteract fertility treatments
interactions.management: Avoid neem leaf, oil, or extract if trying to conceive or undergoing fertility treatment.

interactions.mechanism: Shankhapushpi significantly reduces phenytoin absorption and metabolism — exact mechanism unclear but well-documented in clinical studies
interactions.clinical_effect: Phenytoin blood levels drop by 30-50% — seizures may return or worsen
interactions.management: NEVER combine. This is one of the best-documented dangerous herb-drug interactions. If patient is on phenytoin, avoid all shankhapushpi preparations.

interactions.mechanism: Shankhapushpi has mild hypotensive effects
interactions.clinical_effect: Additive blood pressure lowering
interactions.management: Monitor blood pressure. Generally acceptable.

interactions.mechanism: Brahmi may interact with calcium channels and neurotransmitter systems affecting antiepileptic drug metabolism
interactions.clinical_effect: May alter antiepileptic drug levels — unpredictable effect on seizure control
interactions.management: Use with caution. Monitor drug levels and seizure frequency if combining.

interactions.mechanism: Brahmi modulates GABAergic activity and may enhance CNS depression
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced sedation, excessive drowsiness
interactions.management: Use caution. Avoid in patients requiring alertness. Monitor for excessive sedation.

interactions.mechanism: Brahmi is a cholinesterase inhibitor — additive with anti-Alzheimer drugs
interactions.clinical_effect: Excessive cholinergic stimulation — nausea, vomiting, bradycardia, muscle cramps
interactions.management: Avoid combination or reduce dose of one agent. Monitor for cholinergic excess symptoms.

interactions.mechanism: Gingerols inhibit thromboxane synthetase and platelet aggregation. May inhibit CYP450 enzymes affecting warfarin metabolism.
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk — especially at high ginger doses (>4g/day)
interactions.management: Culinary amounts safe. Avoid ginger supplements (capsules) with blood thinners. Monitor INR with warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Ginger enhances insulin secretion and sensitivity
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced blood sugar lowering — hypoglycemia risk
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose closely. Dietary amounts generally safe.

interactions.mechanism: Ginger inhibits calcium channels — additive with calcium channel blockers
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased blood pressure lowering effect — dizziness, fainting
interactions.management: Monitor blood pressure. May need dose adjustment.

interactions.mechanism: Ginger may affect renal transport of methotrexate
interactions.clinical_effect: May increase methotrexate levels and toxicity
interactions.management: Avoid ginger supplements during methotrexate therapy.

interactions.mechanism: Allicin and ajoene inhibit platelet aggregation. Garlic may inhibit CYP2C9 increasing warfarin levels.
interactions.clinical_effect: Significantly increased bleeding risk. Life-threatening with warfarin.
interactions.management: Avoid garlic supplements with anticoagulants. Culinary amounts generally safe. Monitor INR with warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Garlic strongly induces CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein — reduces antiretroviral drug levels by 50%+
interactions.clinical_effect: Dramatically reduced HIV drug levels — HIV may become uncontrolled, drug resistance may develop
interactions.management: Avoid garlic supplements completely with protease inhibitors.

interactions.mechanism: Garlic enhances insulin secretion and reduces blood glucose
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced hypoglycemic effect — risk of low blood sugar
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose. Adjust medication dose if needed.

interactions.mechanism: Triphala contains vitamin K (from amla) which may affect warfarin. Also mild antiplatelet effects.
interactions.clinical_effect: May alter INR in warfarin patients
interactions.management: Monitor INR closely if taking Triphala with warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Triphala has documented hypoglycemic effects through multiple pathways
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced blood sugar lowering — hypoglycemia risk
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose. Generally beneficial but watch for low blood sugar.

interactions.drug_class: any oral medications requiring consistent absorption
interactions.mechanism: Triphala is a laxative — may reduce absorption of other drugs by speeding GI transit
interactions.clinical_effect: Reduced drug absorption if taken at same time
interactions.management: Take Triphala 2-3 hours away from other medications.

interactions.mechanism: Ursolic acid in Tulsi has antiplatelet properties. Also contains vitamin K which may affect warfarin.
interactions.clinical_effect: Unpredictable effect on warfarin — may increase or decrease anticoagulation
interactions.management: Monitor INR if taking warfarin with significant amounts of Tulsi.

interactions.mechanism: Tulsi has mild hypoglycemic activity
interactions.clinical_effect: Mild additive blood sugar lowering
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose. Generally safe.

interactions.mechanism: Tulsi has mild CNS depressant properties
interactions.clinical_effect: Mildly enhanced sedation
interactions.management: Generally safe at dietary amounts. Avoid large medicinal doses with sedatives.

interactions.mechanism: Shatavari has mild diuretic properties — additive with diuretic medications
interactions.clinical_effect: Excessive fluid loss, electrolyte imbalance, dehydration
interactions.management: Monitor electrolytes and fluid balance.

interactions.mechanism: Shatavari contains phytoestrogens (steroidal saponins) that can mimic or modulate estrogen activity
interactions.clinical_effect: May enhance or compete with hormonal therapies. May reduce tamoxifen effectiveness in estrogen-receptor positive cancers.
interactions.management: Avoid with hormone-sensitive cancers. Discuss with oncologist before use.

interactions.mechanism: Guduchi strongly stimulates immunity — directly counteracts immunosuppression
interactions.clinical_effect: Reduced immunosuppressive effect, risk of autoimmune flares or organ rejection
interactions.management: Avoid in patients on immunosuppressants.

interactions.mechanism: Guduchi lowers blood glucose through multiple mechanisms
interactions.clinical_effect: Hypoglycemia risk when combined with antidiabetics
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose frequently.

interactions.mechanism: Arjuna has cardiac glycoside-like activity and may have additive effects with digoxin on heart rate and contractility
interactions.clinical_effect: Digoxin toxicity symptoms — nausea, arrhythmias, visual disturbances
interactions.management: Avoid combination. Monitor digoxin levels closely if used together.

interactions.mechanism: Arjuna has antihypertensive and cardioprotective effects
interactions.clinical_effect: Additive blood pressure and heart rate lowering — hypotension, bradycardia
interactions.management: Monitor BP and heart rate. May require dose reduction of antihypertensive.

interactions.mechanism: Arjuna has mild antiplatelet properties
interactions.clinical_effect: Mild increase in bleeding risk
interactions.management: Monitor INR if on warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Fenugreek slows glucose absorption and improves insulin sensitivity via 4-hydroxyisoleucine and galactomannan fiber
interactions.clinical_effect: Enhanced blood sugar lowering — hypoglycemia risk
interactions.management: Monitor blood glucose closely. Often used beneficially under medical supervision to reduce antidiabetic drug dose.

interactions.mechanism: Fenugreek contains coumarin compounds that have anticoagulant activity
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.management: Monitor INR with warfarin. Avoid large amounts of fenugreek with blood thinners.

interactions.mechanism: Fenugreek fiber may bind levothyroxine in gut and reduce absorption
interactions.clinical_effect: Reduced thyroid medication absorption
interactions.management: Take levothyroxine at least 2 hours before fenugreek.

interactions.mechanism: Karela contains multiple hypoglycemic agents including charantin (insulin-like), momordicin, and polypeptide-p (plant insulin)
interactions.clinical_effect: Severe hypoglycemia — blood sugar may drop dangerously. Multiple documented cases.
interactions.management: Very close blood glucose monitoring required. Dose adjustment almost always needed. Avoid if not medically supervised.

interactions.mechanism: High doses of karela may have hepatotoxic effects — additive with other liver-affecting drugs
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased liver toxicity risk
interactions.management: Avoid high-dose karela extracts with hepatotoxic medications. Monitor liver function.

interactions.mechanism: Glycyrrhizin causes pseudoaldosteronism — sodium retention, potassium loss, water retention — raising blood pressure
interactions.clinical_effect: High blood pressure, edema, reduced effectiveness of antihypertensives
interactions.management: Avoid licorice supplements with antihypertensives. Deglycyrrhizinated licorice (DGL) is safer.

interactions.mechanism: Licorice causes potassium loss — additive hypokalemia with potassium-wasting diuretics
interactions.clinical_effect: Severe potassium depletion — muscle weakness, cardiac arrhythmias
interactions.management: Avoid licorice root supplements with loop or thiazide diuretics.

interactions.mechanism: Glycyrrhizin inhibits 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase — enhances and prolongs corticosteroid effects
interactions.clinical_effect: Cushing's syndrome-like effects — moon face, weight gain, high blood pressure, diabetes
interactions.management: Avoid combination. If needed, use DGL form.

interactions.mechanism: Licorice-induced hypokalemia increases sensitivity of heart to digoxin toxicity
interactions.clinical_effect: Digoxin toxicity at normal doses — nausea, arrhythmias, vision changes
interactions.management: Avoid licorice with digoxin.

interactions.mechanism: Guggul stimulates thyroid gland and increases T3/T4 levels
interactions.clinical_effect: May raise thyroid levels — risk of hyperthyroid symptoms or reduced methimazole effectiveness
interactions.management: Monitor thyroid function tests. May need dose adjustments.

interactions.mechanism: Guggulsterones have antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.management: Monitor INR with warfarin. Caution with other blood thinners.

interactions.mechanism: Guggul may induce CYP3A4 — reducing statin levels. Also has own cholesterol-lowering effect.
interactions.clinical_effect: Reduced statin effectiveness. But combined cholesterol-lowering may cause additive myopathy risk.
interactions.management: Monitor cholesterol levels. Inform doctor if combining.

interactions.mechanism: Andrographolide inhibits platelet activating factor and platelet aggregation
interactions.clinical_effect: Increased bleeding risk
interactions.management: Avoid with anticoagulants. Monitor INR with warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Andrographis is a potent immunostimulant
interactions.clinical_effect: May counteract immunosuppressive therapy
interactions.management: Avoid in transplant patients.

interactions.mechanism: Andrographis has mild hypotensive activity
interactions.clinical_effect: Additive blood pressure lowering
interactions.management: Monitor blood pressure.
